feedback.problem: The mass density function $\lambda $ of a rectangular iron flat plate that occupies the region $D={(x,y)\,:\,{e}^{2}\le x\le {e}^{6},\,0\le y\le 3}$ is given by $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{{y}^{3}}{x}.$ What is the total mass of the plate?
feedback.worked_solution:
The mass $M$ of a plate that occupies the region $D={(x,y)\,:\,{e}^{2}\le x\le {e}^{6},\,0\le y\le 3}$ with mass density $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{{y}^{3}}{x}$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ={∬}_{D}\frac{{y}^{3}}{x}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we express our double integral as a repeated integral:      

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}\frac{{y}^{3}}{x}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{0}^{3}[{\int }_{{e}^{2}}^{{e}^{6}}\frac{{y}^{3}}{x}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{3}[{\int }_{{e}^{2}}^{{e}^{6}}\frac{{y}^{3}}{x}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{y}^{3}[{\int }_{{e}^{2}}^{{e}^{6}}\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{y}^{3}[\operatorname{ln}⁡x]_{{e}^{2}}^{{e}^{6}}\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{y}^{3}(\operatorname{ln}⁡{e}^{6}-\operatorname{ln}⁡{e}^{2})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}4{y}^{3}\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{3}4{y}^{3}\,\text{d}y & =[{y}^{4}]_{0}^{3} \\  & ={3}^{4}-(0)^{4} \\  & =81\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the mass of the plate is $M=81.$
